title: Replit Pricing in 2026 and How to Estimate Your Bill
summary: Replit pricing includes multiple plans where the total cost exceeds monthly fees. Compare all tiers with their actual expenses to find the right option.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Once you have your measured credit burn, five questions are left, and each comes down to one line on Replit's pricing page. Where a claim could change, the check date is 2026-10-30.


Yes, Replit has a free entry point, but it's a trial of the metered unit, not a place to build indefinitely. The agent's usage is what gets capped, so a free account tells you how fast you burn credits and little else.


Use it to run your measurement cycle before you pay anything. Check date: 2026-10-30.


### Can I cancel Replit or downgrade mid-month?


You can cancel or change plans, but whether the change takes effect immediately or at the end of the billing period decides what you pay for. Credits you've already spent in the cycle are gone either way.


If your burn is front-loaded, such as a heavy first week, downgrading on day ten saves you less than it appears to. Read the billing terms before you click. Check date: 2026-10-30.


### Do unused Replit credits roll over?


Plan as if they don't, unless the vendor page says otherwise. If unused credits expire at the cycle's end, buying a bigger plan than your measured burn means paying for credits you'll never use.


If a given plan or credit pack does carry over, that's a buffer, and you can size the plan a little below your peak month. Check date: 2026-10-30.


If student or education pricing exists, it would be listed apart from the standard plans, so look for it on the pricing page itself or in Replit's education materials.


If you can't find one, price yourself at standard rates. Your measured credit burn is the same whoever you are, so only the rate changes. Check date: 2026-10-30.


### Will deploying an app cost extra on top of my plan?


Treat deployment as its own meter. Hosting a live app is a different kind of usage from the agent writing code, so it can be billed separately from your plan's credits.


Add one line to your estimate for every app you keep running, and note whether each one is always on or only used occasionally. A prototype you forget to shut down keeps costing money after you stop building it. Check date: 2026-10-30.
